summary: Piramal Finance reported a 67% net profit jump to ₹545 crore, Punjab & Sind Bank saw a 40% profit surge, and Ireda and UltraTech Cement also experienced significant profits despite declines in revenue. Just Dial Ltd reported a 9.73% profit drop, while HFCL's profit rose 21%.

facts.statement: Piramal Finance reported a 67% increase in net profit to ₹545 crore for the September quarter, driven by core income growth.
Punjab & Sind Bank saw a 40% profit rise to ₹412 crore, with improved core income and cost-to-income ratio.
Ireda and UltraTech Cement both reported profit increases, with Ireda's profit rising 66.8% to ₹548 crore.

sources.title: Piramal Finance Q2FY27 results: Net profit zooms 67% to ₹545 crore
sources.description:
Non-bank lender Piramal Finance on Monday reported a 67 per cent jump in net profit to Rs 545 crore for the September quarter, helped by core income growth and improvements in costs.
The company's core net interest income grew 35 per cent to Rs 1,530 crore due to a 24 per cent growth in assets under management and a 0.35 per cent expansion in net income margin to 6.5 per cent.
The cost-to-income ratio improved sharply to 52.1 per cent during the reporting quarter from 61.2 per cent, helping the bottom line.
Stressing that the company is uniquely positioned in the NBFC universe, as it does not see a threat to margins amid the rising interest rate environment, its Managing Director and Chief Executive Jairam Sridharan exuded confidence that it will be able to expand NIMs by up to 0.20 per cent over the next year.

sources.title: Punjab & Sind Bank Q2 net profit surges 40% to ₹412 cr on improved income
sources.description:
Punjab & Sind Bank on Saturday reported a 40 per cent jump in net profit to Rs 412 crore for the second quarter ended September 30, helped by improved core income and reduction in bad assets.
The public sector lender posted a net profit of Rs 295 crore in the same period of the previous fiscal.
The bank's total income increased to Rs 3,747 crore in the second quarter from Rs 3,373 crore a year ago, Punjab & Sind Bank said in a regulatory filing.
Interest income rose to Rs 3,394 crore in the September quarter of FY27 from Rs 2,999 crore in the year-ago period.
During the quarter, net interest income rose 22 per cent to Rs 1,162 crore against Rs 950 crore in the second quarter of the last financial year.
Net Interest Income of the bank improved to 2.65 per cent from 2.56 per cent at the end of September 2025.
Cost-to-income ratio reduced to 29.19 per cent compared to 61.87 per cent in the year-ago period.

sources.title: Just Dial Q2 profit declines 9.73% to ₹107.8 cr despite 13% revenue growth
sources.description:
Just Dial Ltd, a leading local search engine, has reported a decline of 9.73 per cent in its consolidated net profit to Rs 107.8 crore in the September quarter of FY27, on a year-on-year basis.
It had posted a net profit of Rs 119.44 crore in the July-September quarter a year ago, according to a regulatory filing.
However, Just Dial's revenue from operations was up 13.11 per cent in the September quarter at Rs 342.82 crore, compared to Rs 303.07 crore in the corresponding quarter a year ago.
Just Dial's total expenses stood at Rs 262.81 crore, up 14.6 per cent YoY in the September quarter.
The company, owned by Reliance Retail Ventures, the retail arm of billionaire Mukesh Ambani-led Reliance Industries Ltd, reported a 5.6 per cent rise in total income to Rs 397.38 crore in the second quarter of FY27.
Share of Just Dial Ltd on Monday settled 2.82 per cent higher at Rs 732.55 apiece on the BSE.

sources.title: Ireda Q2 net profit edges up at ₹554 crore, loan disbursements rise 31%
sources.description:
State-owned Ireda has posted a marginal rise in its standalone net profit to Rs 554 crore for the September quarter, the company said on Monday.
It earned a net profit of Rs 549 crore in the second quarter of the preceding financial year, the Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency (Ireda) said in a statement.
In July-September, the company's revenue from operations rose 14 per cent to Rs 2,345 crore from Rs 2,057 crore a year ago.
Loan disbursement increased 31 per cent to Rs 10,579 crore against Rs 8,062 crore in the year-ago quarter.
Loan book grew 15 per cent to Rs 97,411 crore from Rs 84,477 crore in Q2 FY26.
The company's net worth grew 11 per cent to Rs 14,337 crore during the quarter compared to Rs 12,920 crore a year earlier.

sources.title: HFCL Q2 results: Profit surges to ₹394 crore as AI data centre demand rises
sources.description:
Domestic telecom gear maker HFCL has posted a multi-fold jump in consolidated profit to Rs 394.22 crore in the second quarter ended September 30, 2026, driven by demand for optical fibre cables from AI data centres, the company said in a regulatory filing.
HFCL had posted net profit of around Rs 72 crore in the same period a year ago.
"This is the best-ever quarterly performance in HFCL's history and marks a defining moment in our growth journey.
